candidate_relations.rationale: The greenfield-consumer workflow retrieves and installs an exact release, bootstraps from installed assets, and verifies ownership and authority boundaries, strengthening migration toward project-local installed framework ownership.
The greenfield workflow verifies bootstrap and authority boundaries separately, strengthening the orchestrator rule that bootstrap does not manufacture operator authority.
The shared-orchestration tests return an approval boundary for non-delegable proposals or absent applicable grants instead of manufacturing authority, strengthening bounded grant operations.
Returning to an approval boundary when no grant applies strengthens the workflow-contract rule that workflow intent itself grants no downstream authority.

Restricting installer mutation to the managed root and transaction material while excluding project knowledge, canonical state, authority, and integration strengthens the package boundary excluding project-owned material.
Keeping project knowledge, canonical state, authority, and integration outside installer ownership strengthens the migration requirement to preserve project-owned knowledge and authority.
The bounded-authority-grant contract excludes subdelegation and protected operations from delegation, strengthening the runtime proposition that grants map only into bounded delegable paths.

The delegability classification names exactly the accepted grant-delegable operation classes and keeps Steward authorization, recovery, grant expansion, workflow revision, and materiality non-delegable, strengthening bounded grant operations.

The Rupi end-to-end tests exercise fresh setup and independently bound protected authority mutations, strengthening the requirement that authority ceremonies remain separate from bootstrap lifecycle work.

The greenfield first-invocation specification requires explicit project-owned evidence and stops after immutable candidate submission without reconciliation or admission state, strengthening the Distiller ingestion boundary.
The greenfield first-invocation specification requires provider-boundary raw bytes to be preserved exactly, strengthening the raw-candidate preservation principle.
Requiring creation of an immutable valid candidate submission strengthens the deterministic candidate-submission identity boundary.
The parity report records Phase 1 and Phase 3 candidate artifacts as unchanged, strengthening the baseline requirement that raw candidate artifacts remain preserved across evaluation and parity work.

The Steward-authorization tests reject unauthorized or unavailable targets, bind approval to the exact proposal, fail on projection conflict, and create no semantic or canonical state, strengthening the authorization contract.
The Steward-authorization tests exercise proposal binding and projection failure independently of semantic or canonical state, strengthening the runtime’s separate authorization domain.

The mutation tests verify canonical digest determinism, non-mutating proposal creation, exact proposal approval binding, append/replay behavior, and idempotent retries, strengthening the common mutation substrate.

Defining the CLI as an adapter over shared primitives and orchestration rather than a new semantic or authority layer strengthens the prohibition on consumer-side reinterpretation of normative protocol contracts.
